title: The cornets and trumpets he owned
summary: He describes his cornets and King trumpets and returning to a cornet.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Did you have a cornet when you started or a trumpet?
I wore a cornet. I wore a cornet. I wore two cornet.
What kind of a horn did you like to make?

I just, any, any, any, any, uh, world I had with CG corn was to go then. Then the next, I had a, a king trumpet I got from Mobile. Then the next, I got a, a king trumpet. I had two king trumpets. And I had some other kind of trumpet. I forgot this kind of trumpet that I had. Well, anyway, I was, I used those three and wore them out. I just figured they wasn't suit me so I just got back on, on the CG corn, got me a CG corn. I got it over the lake then now.
You play trumpet now or a cornet?

I have, uh, old, old trumpet. And I still, you know, if I start to play it I'm gonna buy a brand new one. I'm gonna get me a, a Martin. And that'll be the last one. Because they don't make these trumpets gold no more. They make them lack it, you see. Yeah. And they, they don't last. They, they, they smell so bad, you see. Keep, gotta keep them clean all the time. And if you, you shine them too much, you, where's all that lack at all?
